newsitem.title: USA: INSTANT VIEW -- U.S. adds 138,000 news jobs in May.
newsitem.headline: INSTANT VIEW -- U.S. adds 138,000 news jobs in May.

text.p: Following are comments from U.S. economists after the Labor Department reported 138,000 new jobs were created last month down from a revised increase of 323,000 in April. The unemployment rate fell to 4.8 percent versus 4.9 percent in the previous month.
Economists in a Reuters survey had expected 219,000 new jobs to have been created and a jobless rate of 5.0 percent.
DAVID BLITZER, CHIEF ECONOMIST, STANDARD & POOR'S: "Looking at the overall (employment) numbers, it clearly shows the economy is strong."
"The trend rate of job growth is 200,000 or more over the last couple of months... We've got a lot of growth, but it suddenly turns out to be old news, I think."
JAMES PADINHA, ECONOMIST, BRIEFING.COM: "We think the report underscores how tight labor markets are. We had another drop in the jobless rate, we had huge upward revisions to prior months.
"All in all, strong employment. Earnings the prior month were revised up and we got another 0.3 this month which is 3.8 percent year on year.
"Our view is that the argument around the (Federal Open Market Committee) table in July will be more heated and we think a rate increase is more likely now the report is out."

JOSEPH DZIWURA, VICE PRESIDENT AND ECONOMIST, THE SAKURA BANK, LTD: "The nonfarm payroll number was soft. We can explain that by the seasonal adjustment factor. What that tells us is that the June nonfarm payroll number is likely to rebound quite drastically, given that the May number was so soft and depressed by the seasonal factor.
"(The 4.8 percent unemployment rate) raises the possibility that the (Federal Reserve) bank will have to move at the next monetary policy meeting in July."

CAROL STONE, SENIOR ECONOMIST, NOMURA SECURITIES INTERNATIONAL INC: "The trend growth is still firm, even though May is lower. March and April were both revised up and April was revised up substantially. They corrected finally for this 5-week survey period that occurs now and again.
"I think it shows a firm trend there, with 323,000 (jobs) in April; May does not look so weak.
"It does suggest though that forward momentum has moderated. Forward force is somewhat less, but then again the unemployment rate went down.
"I'm not sure that it sends the Fed any different news than that which they had seen."
DAN SETO, SENIOR ECONOMIST, NIKKO SECURITIES CO INTERNATIONAL INC: "The seasonal factors depressed the number. This number had much stronger job gains.
"The unemployment rate will put the Fed on alert. As for payrolls, the labor market is tight ... all indications suggest resurgence of (economic) growth.
"We think the Fed will raise rates in July."
